record.paper_title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them (with appendix: full list of pictures and Python code)
record.context_brief: Error behavior for infinitely smooth data
record.original_question: For the heat equation u_t(t,x)=u_xx(t,x) on the real line, work in the Banach space UC_b(R) of bounded uniformly continuous real functions with the sup norm. Let Lf=f'' generate the heat semigroup e^{tL}. For t=1/2, compare the exact solution e^{tL}u0 with Chernoff products G(t/n)^n u0 and S(t/n)^n u0, where G is first-order Chernoff tangent to L and S is second-order Chernoff tangent to L. Write d_n^G=||e^{tL}u0-G(t/n)^n u0|| and d_n^S=||e^{tL}u0-S(t/n)^n u0||, and estimate log d_n approximately as alpha log n plus beta, where alpha is the order of decreasing error and beta is the free term. Among infinitely smooth initial conditions, what properties beyond infinite differentiability determine the observed order of decreasing error for Chernoff approximation of the heat semigroup? In particular, why do u0(x)=sin x, u0(x)=exp(-x^2), u0(x)=exp(-x^4), and u0(x)=exp(-x^6) produce substantially different pairs of estimated orders (alpha_G, alpha_S), including the case exp(-x^6) where the first-order and second-order Chernoff functions have nearly the same observed order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F = UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ be the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the sup-norm $\|f\| = \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}} |f(x)|$. Let $L\colon\mathrm{Dom}(L)\subset F\to F$ be the operator $Lf=f''$, which generates the heat $C_0$-semigroup $(e^{tL})_{t\ge 0}$ on $F$, namely the semigroup solving the Cauchy problem $u_t(t,x)=u_{xx}(t,x)$, $u(0,\cdot)=u_0$.

Define two families of bounded linear operators on $F$ by
$$(G(t)f)(x) = \tfrac{1}{2} f(x) + \tfrac{1}{4} f(x+2\sqrt{t}) + \tfrac{1}{4} f(x-2\sqrt{t}),$$
$$(S(t)f)(x) = \tfrac{2}{3} f(x) + \tfrac{1}{6} f(x+\sqrt{6t}) + \tfrac{1}{6} f(x-\sqrt{6t}).$$
These are first-order, respectively second-order, Chernoff-tangent to $L$, meaning $G(0)=S(0)=\mathrm{Id}$ and the Taylor expansions of $G(t)f$ and $S(t)f$ at $t=0$ match those of $e^{tL}f$ up to the corresponding order on sufficiently smooth $f$. By Chernoff's theorem, for every $u_0\in F$ and every $t>0$,
$$d_n^G(u_0,t) := \|e^{tL}u_0 - G(t/n)^n u_0\| \to 0, \qquad d_n^S(u_0,t) := \|e^{tL}u_0 - S(t/n)^n u_0\| \to 0$$
as $n\to\infty$. Fix $t=1/2$ and, for a given $u_0$, define the empirical orders $\alpha_G(u_0), \alpha_S(u_0)$ and free terms $\beta_G(u_0), \beta_S(u_0)$ by the linear fits
$$\ln d_n^G \approx \alpha_G \ln n + \beta_G, \qquad \ln d_n^S \approx \alpha_S \ln n + \beta_S.$$

Numerical experiments with the four infinitely differentiable initial conditions
$$u_0(x)=\sin x,\quad u_0(x)=e^{-x^2},\quad u_0(x)=e^{-x^4},\quad u_0(x)=e^{-x^6}$$
yield substantially different pairs $(\alpha_G, \alpha_S)$, including the phenomenon that for $u_0(x)=e^{-x^6}$ the first-order and second-order Chernoff approximations exhibit essentially the same observed order.

Problem: Identify a property (or set of properties) of an initial condition $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})\cap F$, beyond mere $C^\infty$-smoothness, that determines the observed orders $\alpha_G(u_0)$ and $\alpha_S(u_0)$ of decreasing error in the Chernoff approximations of the heat semigroup, and explain in particular why $\sin x$, $e^{-x^2}$, $e^{-x^4}$, and $e^{-x^6}$ produce distinct pairs $(\alpha_G,\alpha_S)$, and why for $e^{-x^6}$ one has $\alpha_G\approx \alpha_S$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open numerical/empirical problem about how features of smooth initial data (beyond $C^\infty$-regularity) control the order of convergence of first- and second-order Chernoff approximations to the heat semigroup. Related rate-of-convergence results exist (e.g. upper/lower estimates in the Chernoff product formula, Galkin–Remizov style speed-of-convergence results for the heat and transport equations), but no source identifies the property determining the empirical $(\alpha_G,\alpha_S)$ for the listed Gaussian-type smooth initial conditions. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations
status_evidence.snippet: An empirical dependence of the order of convergence on the smoothness class of the initial condition is found.
status_evidence.claim: The dependence of observed order on properties of smooth initial data is reported empirically and left as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Speed of convergence of Chernoff approximations for two model examples
status_evidence.snippet: Studies speed of convergence of Chernoff approximations for the heat and transport equations.
status_evidence.claim: Prior related work addresses convergence speed but does not resolve the property-identification question for smooth initial data.

status_evidence.title: Upper and lower estimates for rate of convergence in the Chernoff product formula
status_evidence.snippet: Provides general upper and lower estimates for the rate of convergence in Chernoff's product formula.
status_evidence.claim: General estimates exist, but the specific empirical phenomena for the listed smooth $u_0$ are not explained.
